payload.rationale: Extremely close, high-clash round. PRO anchored a harm-reduction framework and defended it with consistently cited empirics (WHO unsafe-abortion mortality, Guttmacher comparable-rates data, Turnaway Study, #WeCount, McFall v. Shimp, documented Poland/Georgia deaths). CON mounted a strong personhood-plus-causation case and scored real hits: the killing/letting-die distinction, D&E dismemberment as affirmative killing, the duty-to-rescue/special-obligation frame, and turning the Texas JAMA study and the #WeCount concession against PRO. The decisive battleground was the bodily-autonomy analogy. CON repeatedly tried to break it on causation, but PRO produced the load-bearing legal counter (McFall, plus the delegability point: every parental duty CON cited can be discharged by a third party, whereas gestation cannot, and no court has ever compelled organ/tissue donation even from a parent to their own dying child). CON never met the refute-with-citation bar on this central claim — it answered with framework assertion rather than a case compelling internal bodily use — so PRO's strongest line survived to the end. CON's Chile and Texas empirics were directly rebutted (development confound; national totals rose post-Dobbs per #WeCount), while PRO's WHO safety warrant went under-refuted as a causal matter, CON mostly reframing it as 'infrastructure.' PRO edges Matter and Clash; CON earns high marks on Manner/Method and the philosophical personhood extension, keeping it tight.
payload.persuasion_notes: Principle 2 (clash) decided it: both sides engaged directly nearly every ping, but PRO more often overturned CON's specific claims with same-turn citations (McFall, Guttmacher, #WeCount, WHO) rather than bare contradiction, satisfying Principle 3; CON's rebuttals to the bodily-autonomy/organ-donation line leaned on assertion without a citation showing any compelled bodily conscription, weakening them under Principle 3. Principle 4 (dropped arguments): PRO's delegability point and the 'no court compels organ donation even for one's own child' claim were never squarely answered with authority, so they stand. Judged on persuasion not truth (Principle 1), PRO's framework held more of its weight under pressure. Tie-break by higher Clash also favors PRO.
